set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the Southwest Buttress, the Kiwi Route, taking extra slings and gear for anchors. The glacier at the foot of Loki is known for dangerous crevasses.

set.descent_text: Three ways down start from the summit plateau. The usual one crosses the plateau to an obvious rappel point, then rappels on doubled ropes into the gap separating the two towers, and continues down a rotten gully by more rappels to a snowfield. Cross that exposed, possibly icy snowfield to rock on its far side and rappel the slabs and cliffs below from established anchors. The alternative is to rappel the route, but only the upper part is equipped, so most of the anchors lower down would have to be built on a very big face before climbing out of the Parade Glacier.
set.approach: From the Summit Lake shelter, follow the Caribou Glacier northwest to the divide between the Caribou and Parade glaciers. Drop to the Parade Glacier either down the steep snow and ice by the west side of the divide or, on the east side, by rappelling from an anchor close to the saddle. The route begins just right of the big, deep gully above the Parade Glacier; after a heavy snow winter, begin from the right side of the molar-shaped snowfield. The far wall of that gully sheds rock, so do not stop beneath it.

review.notes: Route page gives approach and descent; area pages confirm the Summit Lake/Caribou Glacier access and that the North Peak line is the standard descent. All counts left out. Row says 1 pitch; page says roughly 25-40.
